text: Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze - The candidate must be no older than 70 years old. As for education, when a person submits an application for a job, would he say, “I don’t have a diploma, but I am educated”?! - The Synod must be guided strictly by the statute on governance and administration (28.04.2026, 11:40)

In the criteria, we read that he must be Georgian, must be a monk, must be a member of the Synod, must have an education, and there is an age requirement stating that he must be 40 years old and no older than 70 — this Synod does not have the right to change the governance regulations and must strictly follow the governance statute, - said Archpriest Andria Jაღმაიძე, head of the Patriarchate’s Public Relations Service.
According to him, it is important for the life of the Church that the established order be observed.
“Today, three patriarchal candidates will be selected at the Synod, and the subsequent Synod, an expanded session, will already be held to elect the Patriarch.

In the criteria, we read that he must be Georgian, must be a monk, must be a member of the Synod, must have an education, and there is a reference to age: he must have reached 40 years of age and must be no older than 70.

I am a mathematician; the phrase “no more than 70 years old” means that once you add any amount of time to 70, it is no longer no more than 70. In other words, 70 plus some days and months is already more than 70. As a mathematician, for me, this is completely clear; however, let’s see what decision the synod will make on this.

The second point is that this synod does not have the right to change the regulations on administration and governance and must be guided strictly by the regulations on administration and governance. As for the topic of education, how do you imagine that when a person does not have a diploma and applies for a job vacancy, what will he say—that he does not have a diploma, but is an educated person?! This will not work in any job.

All matters can be subject to interpretation; for example, the question may arise: what does “Georgian” mean? I had a friend, a Yazidi, who was inwardly a very good Georgian; now, if we reason in this way, everything can be called into question. There is also such a concept as “hidden monks,” and here, in the criterion, it says monk—“hidden monk” means that he has not been tonsured, but lives as a monk; that is, everything can be subject to interpretation. So I think it is very important for the life of the Church that the rule that has been defined be observed.
“We have already received information about the delegates from most of the dioceses,” said Andria Jagmaidze.
